Comparing groups with different sample sizes

Source: vignettes/07_unequal_sample_size.Rmd
07_unequal_sample_size.Rmd
library(keRnel)
library(BayesOmics)
library(ggplot2)

One condition is cheap to sample, the other is rare or expensive – the two groups end up with very different replicate counts. This is fully supported: a group’s posterior scale is n_obs + lambda_0, using only that group’s own replicate count. The only real requirement is that both groups share the same Input positions (so they share the same kernel matrix and can be compared at all) – nothing requires the same N.

Simulate an unbalanced design

3 replicates for Rare, 15 for Abundant:

set.seed(7)
kern_true <- variance_kernel(variance = 10) * se_kernel(length_scale = 80)
data <- simu_db_kernel(
  kernel        = kern_true,
  nb_id         = 6,
  nb_group      = 2,
  nb_sample     = c(3, 15),
  diff_group    = 0.8,
  var_sample    = 5,
  range_input   = c(0, 200),
  group_labels  = c("Rare", "Abundant"),
  integer_input = TRUE,
  input_grid    = TRUE
)
ggplot(data, aes(Input, Output, color = Group, group = interaction(Group, Sample))) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_point(size = 1)

Rare has visibly fewer lines than Abundant – the asymmetry the rest of this example works through.

Fit and compare, as usual 

kern <- variance_kernel(variance = 1) * se_kernel(length_scale = 50) +
  white_noise_kernel(noise = 1)
g1         <- data[data$Group == "Rare", ]
prior_mean <- mean(g1$Output)
hp_opt     <- fit_kernel(kern, g1, prior_mean = prior_mean, prior_cov = 1)
kern_opt   <- kupdate(kern,
                       variance     = hp_opt[["variance"]],
                       length_scale = hp_opt[["length_scale"]],
                       noise        = hp_opt[["noise"]])
posterior  <- posterior_mean(data, kern_opt, mu_0 = prior_mean, lambda_0 = 1)

Each group’s own scale reflects its own sample size:

c(Rare = posterior$groups$Rare$scale, Abundant = posterior$groups$Abundant$scale)
#>     Rare Abundant 
#>        4       16
group_diff(posterior)
#> Metric: ovl_metric(n_mc = 2000) 
#> 
#>               Rare  Abundant
#> Rare     1.0000000 0.0282199
#> Abundant 0.0282199 1.0000000

Rare has scale 4 (3 + lambda_0), Abundant has scale 16 (15 + lambda_0) – Rare’s posterior is proportionally wider, and the OVL above already accounts for that difference correctly.

Visualize the width difference 

samples <- sample_posterior(posterior, n = 2000)
plot_posterior_overlap(samples, group1 = "Rare", group2 = "Abundant",
                        id = unique(samples$ID)[1])

Rare’s density is visibly wider than Abundant’s – fewer replicates, less certainty about the mean – even though both are centered where the simulated effect places them.

Takeaways

  • Unequal nb_sample across groups needs no special handling: fit and compare exactly as in the balanced case.
  • What is required is that both groups are measured at the same Input positions – not the same replicate count.
